user.title: Lighting Console
user.description: Set up the Lighting Console. Nothing to configure here — the rig and your shows are managed from the console card itself. To pair a Hue bridge for effects, use Reconfigure afterwards.

reconfigure.title: Hue bridge
reconfigure.description: The address of the Hue bridge the console should use for effects. Only genuine Hue colour lights in an entertainment area can be driven by effects; everything else in the rig is controlled through Home Assistant as normal.

link.title: Press the link button
link.description:
Press the round button on top of {bridge}, then select Submit within 30 seconds.

This grants the console its own application key and a client key. The client key is what lets effects stream to the bridge — without it, effects could never run.

error.cannot_connect: The bridge did not answer at that address. Check the address and that Home Assistant can reach it.
error.not_a_bridge: Something answered at that address, but it is not a Hue bridge.
error.link_button_not_pressed: The link button was not pressed in time. Press the round button on top of the bridge, then select Submit within 30 seconds.
error.pairing_failed: Pairing failed. Check the Home Assistant log for the reason the bridge gave.
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. Check the Home Assistant log.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Lighting Console is already set up. Only one console instance is supported.

init.title: Effect performance
init.description:
How many effect commands the console may have in flight to the Hue bridge at once.

Lower is more responsive to Stop and the next cue; higher keeps the bridge busier, so a fast strobe looks smoother. The default of 2 stops well within a second. Raise it only if effects look sluggish on a large rig, and remember that every extra frame in flight is extra delay before the rig goes still.
